true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Duplicate `self.downsize` definition makes the 4-argument version dead code and breaks its callers

The file now defines `OptimizedImage.downsize` twice: once at line 145 with the signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and again at line 149 with `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby has no method overloading — the second definition silently replaces the first, so the 4-argument version is unreachable. Worse, any existing or future caller using the old 4-argument form (`downsize(from, to, width, height)`) will now have `height` bound to `opts`, and `!!opts[:allow_animation]` in `optimize` will raise a TypeError (no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer) at runtime instead of resizing. The leftover dead definition also misleads readers about the real contract. One of the two definitions should be removed and all callers migrated to a single signature.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side upload size validation hardcoded to 10 MB, ignoring configured per-type limits

`validateUploadedFile` previously enforced `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so the composer blocked oversized files before upload using the admin-configured image/attachment limits. It now uses a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. On sites with lower configured limits, users pass client validation and only fail later with a server error; on sites with higher limits (e.g. large attachments allowed), users are incorrectly blocked at 10 MB. The error message also now interpolates the raw value 10240 as `max_size_kb`. The client should keep reading the site setting; the server-side downsizing added in this PR handles the oversized-image case.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
413 error message reports a hardcoded 10 MB limit instead of the actual configured limit

In `displayErrorForUpload`, the 413 handler now shows `I18n.t('post.errors.file_too_large', { max_size_kb: 10 * 1024 })` instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. Users will be told the limit is 10240 KB even when the site setting (and the web server limit that actually produced the 413) is different, and the raw kilobyte number is shown unformatted. The message should use the real configured limit.

API download limit hardcoded to 10 MB ignores site settings and applies to all types

The URL-based upload path for API clients changed from `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` to a hardcoded `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`. This branch handles any upload `type`, not just images, so an admin who raised `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10 MB still cannot pull larger files via the API URL flow (the download is silently truncated/rejected at 10 MB and `rescue nil` swallows it, yielding a confusing nil-tempfile failure), while an admin who lowered limits gets no benefit from the cap at this layer. If the intent was only to accommodate images that will later be downsized, the limit should still derive from a setting (or at least only relax for image types).

Downsize retry loop ignores conversion failures

The loop `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` never checks the boolean return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize`. If the conversion fails (corrupt image, unsupported format such as SVG written to an extensionless tempfile path so ImageMagick cannot determine the output format, missing binary), each iteration simply re-runs the same failing `convert` plus `ImageOptim` up to 5 times, wasting CPU in the deferred job and logging nothing about the upload-level failure. The loop should break (and ideally log) when `downsize` returns false.

Downsizing large animated GIFs silently destroys their animation

The new downsize path calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. Inside `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated branch is chosen only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but `from` here is the upload tempfile path (e.g. `/tmp/RackMultipart...`), which has no file extension, so the regex never matches. The code therefore falls through to `downsize_instructions`, which runs `convert #{from}[0] ...` — the `[0]` selector flattens the image to its first frame. A user uploading a large animated GIF will have the animation permanently discarded with no warning, even though `allow_animation` was explicitly passed. The animated-detection should be based on the original filename/content type, not the tempfile path.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil

The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If an `EmbeddableHost` is built without a host (e.g. the admin controller receives a request missing `embeddable_host[host]`, or code does `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?`), `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `return unless self.host` (or `self.host = self.host.to_s`) and add a presence validation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
update and destroy raise NoMethodError for an unknown host id instead of 404

`update` and `destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then use the result without a nil check: `update` passes nil into `save_host`, where `host.host = ...` raises NoMethodError, and `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on nil. A request for a deleted or bogus id returns a 500. Both actions should raise `Discourse::NotFound` (or use `find`) when the record is missing.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
record_for_host does not downcase the incoming host and cannot match hosts saved with a port

`record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` where `host` is `uri.host`. Ruby's URI parser preserves the case of the host (it is only downcased by `#normalize`), so a referer like `http://EVILTROUT.COM/page` will not match the stored lowercase `eviltrout.com` — the comparison should be against `host.downcase`. Additionally, the host validation regex on line 2 permits an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), so an admin can save `example.com:3000`, but `uri.host` strips the port, meaning such a record can never match and embedding from that host is always rejected. Either reject ports in validation or include the port in the lookup.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are inserted raw, keeping scheme/path that lookups will never match

The old `embeddable_hosts` setting explicitly supported values like `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234` (the old specs set exactly those values). The new `EmbeddableHost` model strips the scheme and path in a `before_validation` callback, but the migration inserts the old values with raw SQL, bypassing the model entirely. After migration, rows contain e.g. `https://example.com/1234`, while `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `uri.host` (`example.com`) against the stored value, so every previously configured host that included a scheme or path silently stops being allowed — existing embedded comment installs break until an admin manually re-saves each host.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped

`spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines all the category fabricators (`category`, `diff_category`, `happy_category`, `private_category`). The Fabrication gem loads every file in the directory so the test suite still runs, but the file names no longer match their contents — the new file's content belongs in `category_fabricator.rb` and vice versa.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration interpolates setting values directly into SQL without escaping

The migration builds INSERT statements with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. `h` comes from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting, which was free text; a host entry containing a single quote will produce invalid SQL and fail the migration mid-way (and in principle allows SQL injection). Use `sanitize`/`quote` or a bound parameter instead of string interpolation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when the embed_category site setting has no DB row

The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. Site settings only have a row in the `site_settings` table when an admin has overridden the default; on any install where `embed_category` was never changed from its empty default (or was set to a blank/non-matching value so the join returns nothing), the result set is empty, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and blocking the deploy. The result needs a nil check before indexing (the same pattern is repeated on line 15 for `uncategorized_category_id`).

false_positives.candidate:
New admin endpoints have no request specs

The specs added for `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (and `Admin::EmbeddingController`) only assert the class is a subclass of AdminController. There is no coverage for create/update/destroy behavior — authorization (non-staff rejected), the default-to-uncategorized category fallback, validation error rendering, deleting a host, or the embedding show endpoint. These endpoints implement the core of the feature (including the nil-record crashes noted above) and currently have zero functional coverage.

No uniqueness constraint or validation on host

Neither the model nor the migration enforces uniqueness of `host`, so admins can create duplicate rows for the same host pointing at different categories. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` then uses `.first`, making the category chosen for imported embedded topics arbitrary, and the admin UI shows conflicting duplicate rows. Add a unique index plus `validates_uniqueness_of :host, case_sensitive: false`.

Plural *_ids hydration produces arrays of undefined and deletes the raw ids even when nothing was resolved

In `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch maps `foo_ids` through `_lookupSubType` and then unconditionally sets `obj[plural] = hydrated` and deletes `obj[k]`. Unlike the singular branch (which only assigns and deletes when a hydrated object was actually found), this branch assigns even when `_lookupSubType` returned undefined for some or all ids — producing e.g. `colors: [undefined, undefined]` and destroying the original `color_ids` data. Any payload containing a plural id array whose collection is missing from the root (or partially missing ids) is silently corrupted. It should skip the assignment when nothing resolved, and ideally compact/filter unresolved ids; the `|| []` on the map result is also dead code since `map` always returns an array.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row

`tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil — any logged-in user can visit `/t/<id>/unsubscribe` for a topic they have never read, posted in, or been emailed about, in which case no topic_users row exists. The very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising NoMethodError and producing a 500. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)` (which upserts) or handle the nil case explicitly.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Direct TopicUser save bypasses bookkeeping done by TopicUser.change

The unsubscribe action sets `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of using `TopicUser.change`. As a result `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not updated (so there is no audit trail of when/why the level changed) and no MessageBus `notification_level_change` event is published, leaving the user's other open browser tabs showing a stale notification state for the topic.

No request specs for the new topics#unsubscribe action

The PR adds a new state-changing controller action (notification level changes, slug-mismatch 301 redirect, nil-TopicUser case, login requirement) but the only spec change is adding an `unsubscribe_url` option to an existing message builder spec. There are no request/controller specs covering the unsubscribe flow, which is how the nil TopicUser crash and the GET-mutation behavior slipped through.

Unsubscribe mutates state on a GET request (CSRF / link-prefetch) The new `unsubscribe` action is routed as GET (`get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in config/routes.rb) and is added to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`, so a plain browser GET with only the session cookie changes the user's TopicUser notification_level. This violates safe-GET semantics in two ways: (1) any third-party page can silently unsubscribe/mute a logged-in user from an arbitrary topic via `` since topic ids are enumerable; (2) mail clients and security scanners (Outlook SafeLinks, Gmail prefetch, corporate link checkers) routinely follow links in emails, so the unsubscribe link in the notification email can be triggered without the user ever clicking it, silently muting the topic. The mutation should require a POST/PUT with CSRF protection, with the GET page only rendering the confirmation UI.

topicUnsubscribe route is shadowed by topic.fromParamsNear wildcard

The new route `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' })` is declared after `this.resource('topic', { path: '/t/:slug/:id' }, ...)` whose child route `fromParamsNear` has path `/:nearPost`. Ember matches routes in declaration order, so `/t/some-slug/123/unsubscribe` matches `topic.fromParamsNear` with `nearPost = "unsubscribe"` and the topicUnsubscribe route is never reached. The client then runs topic-from-params' setupController with a garbage nearPost, loading the topic stream instead of the unsubscribe confirmation page. The route must be declared before the topic resource (or nested with an explicit path that takes precedence).

unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url; callers without it will raise

config/locales/server.en.yml changed `unsubscribe_link` to include `[click here](%{unsubscribe_url})`. MessageBuilder calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` (here and in html_part) whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, but `unsubscribe_url` is only present in template_args if the caller passed it. Any existing or future caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to build the email. Either make the interpolation optional (fall back to the old text when unsubscribe_url is absent) or guard it in MessageBuilder.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validator performs a database write, and signups double-count match statistics

EmailValidator.validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value), which increments match_count, sets last_match_at, and saves the BlockedEmail record — i.e., running model validations now has a write side effect. This is fragile in itself (validations can run in contexts where writes are unexpected), and it produces incorrect statistics in the main signup flow: UsersController#create calls user.valid? (line 168, app/controllers/users_controller.rb) to decide whether to contact the Discourse hub, and then user.save runs validations again, so a single blocked signup attempt increments match_count twice. The stats update should be moved out of the validation path (e.g., done once in the controller) or de-duplicated.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, allowing trivial bypass

BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact-match query (BlockedEmail.where(email: email)) against the raw email string passed in from the user record, and User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] without downcasing or stripping. The fabricator and any manually curated blocklist entries will be lowercase, so a signup with 'BAD@spammers.org' will not match a blocklist entry for 'bad@spammers.org', even though those are the same mailbox in practice. Anyone blocked can re-register (or re-attempt) by simply changing the case of their address, defeating the feature this PR adds. The email should be normalized (e.g., Email.downcase(email).strip) both when storing BlockedEmail rows and when looking them up.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
Moved whitelist/blacklist domain logic has no test coverage

The PR moves the email_domains_whitelist / email_domains_blacklist restriction logic out of User#email_validator into the new EmailValidator class, and removes the old User model code. The new spec only exercises the BlockedEmail branch (stubbing BlockedEmail.should_block?); there are no tests asserting that a non-whitelisted domain is rejected, that a blacklisted domain is rejected, or that an allowed domain passes. If the moved logic broke (e.g., the elsif precedence between whitelist and blacklist, or regex construction in email_in_restriction_setting?), nothing in this PR's tests would catch it. Tests covering the whitelist and blacklist branches should be added (or the old user email-restriction specs kept/pointed at the new validator).

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check accepts origins that merely start with the forum URL

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring check, not an origin comparison. If discourseUrl is 'https://forum.example.com', then a message from origin 'https://forum.example.com.evil.com' passes the check (indexOf returns 0), so any site whose origin begins with the forum's origin string can send messages to the embed script. Today the only handled message resizes the iframe, so impact is limited to layout manipulation, but the check is wrong and will silently extend to any future message types. It should compare e.origin against the parsed origin of discourseUrl exactly.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
i.content is nil for feeds without content:encoded, crashing the hourly job

SimpleRSS only populates `item.content` when the feed entry has a `<content:encoded>` (or `<content>`) element. Plain RSS 2.0 feeds that only provide `<description>` — which is extremely common — will have `i.content == nil`, so `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError. The exception aborts the whole PollFeed run (and since it is raised inside the hourly scheduled job, every subsequent run fails the same way), so no topics are ever imported from such feeds. The code should fall back to `i.description` when `i.content` is blank.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Adding a column with a default rewrites and locks the posts table

`add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` on PostgreSQL versions prior to 11 rewrites the entire posts table to materialize the default, taking an access-exclusive lock for the duration. On a large forum this can block all reads/writes to posts for a long time during deploy. The safer pattern for that era is to add the column without a default, backfill in batches, then set the default and NOT NULL constraint.

Check-then-create race in TopicEmbed.import crashes concurrent jobs

import looks up `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, when absent, creates the topic, post, and TopicEmbed row inside a transaction. Two RetrieveTopic jobs (or a poll plus a retrieve) for the same URL running concurrently can both see no existing embed and both try to create; the unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url makes the loser's `TopicEmbed.create!` raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, rolling back the just-created topic/post and failing the Sidekiq job (with retries). The race should be handled, e.g. by rescuing RecordNotUnique and re-reading the existing embed.

Editing an already-released migration to add force: true is ineffective and dangerous

This migration was already merged and run by existing installations; changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` will never execute for anyone who already migrated, so whatever problem the edit was meant to fix silently persists for them. Worse, `force: true` drops the existing table before recreating it — for any environment where this migration has not yet run but the table exists with data, running it will destroy that data. If the table needs to be recreated, that must be done in a new migration.

Per-URL retrieval throttle is trivially bypassed, enabling unauthenticated fetch amplification

The anonymous-accessible GET /embed/best endpoint enqueues a RetrieveTopic job for any embed_url, which makes the server perform an outbound HTTP fetch of that URL (TopicRetriever -> TopicEmbed.import_remote -> open(url)). The only protection is a 60-second Redis throttle keyed on the exact URL string (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`). An attacker can bypass it indefinitely by appending unique query strings (e.g. ?r=1, ?r=2, ...) to the same page on the embeddable host, causing the forum to hammer the configured embeddable host with unbounded fetches — a denial-of-service amplification against the very site the forum operator embeds. The throttle should be normalized (e.g. keyed on host/path, or a global rate limit) and import_remote should have timeouts and size limits.

RSS/feed HTML is stored and rendered without any sanitization (stored XSS)

poll_feed takes the raw HTML from each feed item (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and passes it to TopicEmbed.import, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Post#cook (app/models/post.rb) returns `raw` verbatim for raw_html posts, skipping the entire rendering and sanitization pipeline, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (the main app also serves cooked HTML to clients). Nothing ever sanitizes this content, so a feed entry containing `<script>` or event-handler attributes becomes stored XSS executed for every forum visitor and embed viewer. The forum trusts the configured feed URL, but a compromised or hostile blog feed would fully compromise the forum. The imported HTML should be run through Sanitize (already a dependency) before being stored.

absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs

URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` start with '/', so they match the `href.start_with?('/')` branch and are rewritten to `http://<feed host>//cdn.example.com/img.png`, which is broken. Protocol-relative hrefs and srcs are common in feed content; they will all 404 after import. The rewrite should skip values starting with '//'.

setnx + expire is not atomic; a crash between them permanently blocks retrieval of the URL

retrieved_recently? does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` as two separate commands. If the process crashes or the Redis connection drops between the two, the key is set with no TTL, and that embed URL will be treated as 'retrieved recently' forever — the topic will never be imported. A single atomic SET with EX (or setex) avoids the window.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items mixin emits a nonexistent -ms-align-items property and mismatched old-box values

The new align-items mixin emits '-ms-align-items: $alignment', which is not a real CSS property in any browser (IE10 implements '-ms-flex-align', which the mixin already includes) — it is dead code that suggests IE support the mixin doesn't actually verify. Additionally, '-webkit-box-align' (2009 flexbox) only accepts start/end/center/baseline/stretch; it does not accept 'flex-start'/'flex-end', so any future caller passing those values will get no alignment at all in browsers that fall back to 'display: -webkit-box'. Similarly the flexbox mixin emits 'display: -moz-box' but there is no accompanying '-moz-box-align', so the old-Firefox fallback is only half implemented. Either trim the unsupported fallbacks or add the correct value mapping.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
Header .contents is now a non-wrapping flex row with no shrink/overflow handling

.d-header .contents now uses display:flex with align-items:center but no flex-wrap (defaults to nowrap) and no min-width:0 on the items. Previously .title floated left and .panel floated right, so on narrow viewports content could drop/reflow; as flex items, .title, .extra-info-wrapper (which contains the topic title text and can be long) and .panel cannot wrap, and modern flex items refuse to shrink below their min-content size without min-width:0. On narrow screens or with a long topic title shown in the docked header, this can cause horizontal overflow or squished/overlapping header elements instead of graceful reflow. Consider adding min-width:0 plus text-overflow handling to .extra-info-wrapper/.title, or an appropriate flex-wrap/flex-shrink strategy.

Leftover .valign-helper rule is meaningless inside the new flex container

.valign-helper (display:inline-block; height:100%; vertical-align:middle) was a hack for vertically centering header content under the old float layout. Now that .contents is a flex container with align-items:center, this element becomes a flex item: vertical-align does not apply to flex items and height:100% resolves against an indefinite container height (auto). The rule is dead weight from an incomplete refactor and should be removed along with the corresponding element in the header template if it is no longer needed.

button float:right inside .small-action is ignored now that the container is flex

The PR makes .small-action a flex container (@include flexbox()). Floats have no effect on flex items, so the 'button { float: right; }' rule inside .small-action (and the leftover 'float: left' on .topic-avatar) is now dead. false_positives.candidate:
Fallback locales are only loaded for controller requests, so fallbacks silently fail in jobs/mailers

Fallback loading is triggered solely by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Because the translate accelerator lazy-loads only `config.locale` (see `translate` in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb), any translation performed outside a web request — Sidekiq jobs, user notification emails, scheduled tasks — will have the current locale's file loaded but never the fallback chain (site default locale and :en). In those contexts a key missing from the user's locale will render as 'translation missing' instead of falling back to the default/English string, so the feature only works for HTTP requests and silently no-ops elsewhere. The fallback loading should happen inside the translation path (e.g., in `load_locale`/`translate` or `I18n.with_locale`) rather than in a controller before_filter.

FallbackLocaleList#[] recomputes the chain on every translation lookup

`I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` for every translation that reaches the backend (which is all translations with interpolation arguments, since the LRU cache only covers the no-args path). The overridden `[]` performs a `SiteSetting.default_locale` lookup, allocates a symbol via `to_sym`, allocates and `uniq`s an array on every call, even though the result only changes when `default_locale` changes. On translation-heavy pages this is pure per-call overhead. Consider memoizing the computed list and invalidating it when the default_locale setting changes.

No tests for the new fallback ordering and loading behavior

This PR introduces a custom fallback chain (user locale → site default locale → :en), replaces the global `I18n.fallbacks` object with a custom `FallbackLocaleList`, moves pluralization setup between initializers, and adds `ensure_loaded!` to the translation accelerator, but changes no spec files (the PR description is also just the placeholder 'Test 9'). There is no coverage verifying that a key missing in the user locale resolves to the default locale and then to English, that `FallbackLocaleList#[]` behaves correctly when the user locale equals the default locale, or that fallback locale files actually get loaded. A regression here would surface as untranslated UI strings and would be easy to miss without tests.

Translation LRU cache key does not account for the fallback chain, so cached results go stale when default_locale changes or differs per site

The accelerator caches no-argument translations under `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. Before this change, the translation for a given key+locale depended only on that locale's file; now it also depends on the fallback chain, which includes `SiteSetting.default_locale` (see `FallbackLocaleList#[]` in config/initializers/i18n.rb). The cache is only cleared by `I18n.reload!`, which a site-setting change does not trigger. Consequences: (1) after an admin changes the site default locale, keys missing in a user's locale keep serving strings from the old default locale until the process restarts; (2) on multisite installs where different sites share the process and backend but have different `default_locale` values, a fallback result cached for one site is served to another site with a different default locale, producing wrong-language output. The cache key needs to incorporate the effective fallback list (or the cache must be invalidated when `default_locale` changes).

false_positives.candidate:
Hardcoded 1000-span eviction ignores max_segment_spans and silently drops spans

The new eviction `if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)` hardcodes 1000, while `SpansBuffer` still accepts a configurable `max_segment_spans` (default 1001) that is now never used — the Python-side check that dropped oversized segments with a `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric and error log was removed from `_load_segment_data`. Consequences: (1) the configured limit is silently ignored, (2) spans are evicted silently instead of the segment being dropped with an error, so downstream consumers receive incomplete segments presented as complete, and (3) `zpopmin` evicts the lowest-scored (earliest `end_timestamp_precise`) spans, which can include the segment's root span, changing flush semantics. `max_segment_spans` should either be passed into the script or removed.

KeyError on payloads missing end_timestamp_precise crashes the batch

`Span(..., end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"], ...)` is a new hard dictionary access. The consumer only `cast`s the decoded JSON to `SpanEvent` and performs no schema validation, so any message lacking this field (older Relay payloads, malformed messages, spillover replays) raises `KeyError`, which fails the entire batch and causes it to be reprocessed in a crash loop. Previously this field was never read. Use `val.get(...)` with a fallback (e.g., 0 or the batch timestamp) if the field is not guaranteed to be present.

Redirect-follow limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 without rationale

The redirect-chasing loop was lowered from `for i = 0, 10000` to `for i = 0, 1000`, and the old comment documenting the consequence ('segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly') was deleted. Segment trees whose redirect chain exceeds 1000 hops will now silently stop being merged — children will stay in a separate set and be flushed as their own (incomplete) segment. If the reduction is intentional for latency, the trade-off should at least be documented; otherwise deep traces lose spans relative to the old behavior.

SET→ZSET migration breaks in-flight buffered segments with WRONGTYPE errors

The script and the Python producer switch segment buffer keys from Redis SETs (`sadd`/`scard`/`sunionstore`) to sorted sets (`zadd`/`zcard`/`zunionstore`), but existing keys in Redis written by the old code are still SETs. Calling `zcard`/`zunionstore` on a SET key (and likewise `p.zadd` in `SpansBuffer.process_spans`) raises a WRONGTYPE error, which aborts the Lua script and fails the whole batch of `EVALSHA` calls. During a rolling deploy — and for up to `redis_ttl` afterwards — all traces with segments buffered by the old code will cause consumer errors and those spans will not be buffered. There is no type check or migration path (e.g., probing with `type`/`object encoding`, or a key version bump).

Upsampling decision uses outer `dataset`/raw request query instead of `scoped_dataset` and the actual query string

Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` closes over the outer `dataset` variable and the helper reads `request.GET['query']` directly, ignoring both the `scoped_dataset` parameter and the `query` argument passed to `_get_event_stats`. In the dashboard-widget split path, `_get_event_stats` is invoked with modified queries — e.g. `(<query>) AND !event.type:transaction` for the errors split (with scoped_dataset=discover) and `(<query>) AND event.type:transaction` for the transactions split — and with a scoped_dataset that can differ from the outer dataset (e.g. discover while the outer dataset is metrics_performance). As a result the upsampling transformation is applied or skipped based on the wrong dataset and the wrong query text: the transactions-only split query can get upsampled counts (wrong numbers) and the errors-only split query can fail to get upsampled counts (undercounted). The check should use `scoped_dataset` and the `query` parameter actually being executed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

false_positives.candidate:
Accidentally committed git submodule ('sentry-repo') pointing at the repo's own base commit

The PR adds a file `sentry-repo` containing `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` — a gitlink (embedded submodule) referencing the base commit of this very repository. This looks like a local checkout accidentally committed as a submodule. It adds a bogus gitlink to the tree, will break or slow down `git clone --recursive` / CI checkout steps (the submodule has no .gitmodules entry), and has nothing to do with the feature. It should be removed before merging.

Substring match treats negated queries like `!event.type:error` as error-focused

`_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the raw query string contains the substring "event.type:error". A query that explicitly *excludes* errors, e.g. `!event.type:error` (the standard way to query non-error/transaction events in discover), also contains that substring, so it will be classified as error-focused and `count()` will be rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` over transaction rows, where sample_weight is absent/zero — returning wrong (likely zero) counts. Similarly, a query merely mentioning the field in another context (e.g. inside a quoted message search) triggers upsampling. The check should parse the query or at least exclude negated occurrences instead of doing a raw substring search.

Top-level eligibility function and its 60s caching behavior are never tested

The unit tests exercise the private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) but never call the public entry point `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. That function contains the PR's riskiest new logic — the cache key construction, the cache-hit short-circuit, and the combination of cached eligibility with the per-request dataset check — so regressions there (e.g. caching False forever, key collisions across project sets, ignoring the dataset check on cache hits) would not be caught by these tests.

invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code; allowlist changes are stale for up to 60s with no way to invalidate, and the docstring contradicts the cache

`invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined and documented as the mechanism to call 'when the allowlist configuration changes', but nothing in the codebase calls it, so allowlist edits always take up to 60 seconds to take effect with no escape hatch. Additionally, the docstring on `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` claims it 'reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time ... to ensure we always have the latest configuration state', which is directly contradicted by the 60-second result cache in the only caller. Either wire the invalidation into the option-change path or fix the misleading documentation.

upsampled_count is registered as a public function, exposing it to arbitrary user queries

Unlike the neighboring private SnQL functions (e.g. the one above it with `private=True`), `upsampled_count` is registered without `private=True`, making it usable by any user in arbitrary Discover queries and datasets. Against datasets/contexts where the `sample_weight` column does not exist (transactions, etc.) this produces Snuba query errors surfaced to users, and it exposes an internal implementation detail as part of the public query API. It should be marked private and explicitly allowed only where the upsampling transformation injects it.

upsampled_count sums sample_weight with no NULL fallback, zeroing out events stored without a weight

The new `upsampled_count` SnQL function compiles to `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` and the surrounding comments state it 'assumes sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects'. That assumption does not hold: allowlisting is per-project, but error events ingested *before* the project was allowlisted (or ingested without client sampling) have no sample_weight, and stats queries routinely cover historical time ranges. For rows where sample_weight is NULL, `sum` will either ignore them or return NULL (which `toInt64` turns into 0), so `count()` on an allowlisted project will silently undercount — showing 0 or fewer errors than actually occurred — for any time bucket containing older events. The aggregate should fall back to 1 for missing weights, e.g. `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
fetch_error_details misaligns error IDs with nodestore results via zip

In fetch_error_details, the code does `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by node id whose iteration order follows the backend's query order, not the order of `error_ids`, and any missing node is simply absent from the dict. If any one error event is missing from nodestore (expired/deleted), every subsequent pairing shifts by one, so each ErrorEvent gets the wrong `id` attached to the wrong event's title/message, and the final error_ids entries are silently dropped. The result is error context injected into the Seer summary prompt with incorrect event IDs and missing errors. The lookup should map back by node id instead of relying on positional zip, e.g. iterate `zip(error_ids, node_ids)` and read `events.get(node_id)`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feature-flagged table widget path renders hardcoded empty table, discarding real query results

In WidgetCardChart.tableResultComponent, when the organization has the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` instead of the actual `tableResults`/`result.data`/`result.meta` that were just fetched. If this flag is ever enabled for an organization, every table widget on their dashboards will render a permanently empty table (columns is an empty array, so no headers or rows render at all), and the loading/error/fieldAlias handling in the existing SimpleTableChart path is bypassed entirely. This is clearly a placeholder that should not be merged as-is; either wire the real `result.data`/`result.meta`/fields into TableWidgetVisualization or don't branch on the flag yet.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validation uses truthiness, so age=0 bypasses it

BrowserReportSerializer.validate_timestamp checks `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and validate_age checks `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")` to enforce that the two fields are mutually exclusive. Because `age` is an IntegerField, a report containing `"age": 0` together with a `timestamp` passes both validators (0 is falsy), accepting a report that mixes the two spec formats the serializer is explicitly designed to reject. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` / `is not None` instead of truthiness.

true_positives.golden_comment: Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Assemble analytics event recorded before feature-flag and schema validation

The new `analytics.record('preprod_artifact.api.assemble', ...)` call is placed at the top of `post`, before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check (which returns 404) and before `validate_preprod_artifact_schema` (which returns 400). As a result the analytics event fires for requests from orgs without the feature and for malformed requests, inflating the metric with failed/no-op calls and making it unusable as a measure of actual assemble usage. Move the record call below the feature check and schema validation (or after the task is successfully enqueued).

In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

false_positives.candidate:
Falsy check on custom cell renderer causes valid falsy renders to be discarded

In renderDefaultBodyCell (and the same pattern in renderDefaultHeadCell at line 32), the custom renderer result is checked with `if (cell) { return cell; }` before falling back to the default renderer. The documented contract is that returning `undefined` opts into the fallback, but a custom renderer that legitimately returns `0`, `""`, or `null` (e.g. a cell that intentionally renders an empty value) will be silently replaced by the default field renderer's output, producing incorrect cell content. Check `cell !== undefined` instead so only an explicit undefined triggers the fallback.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Read-modify-write race lets the same backup code authenticate concurrent requests

Backup code consumption is decrypt → indexOf → set slot to null → re-encrypt → save, with no locking or atomic update. Two concurrent login requests using the same backup code can both read the pre-consumption ciphertext, both find the code, and both succeed before either writes back. One-time-use of a backup code is therefore not guaranteed under concurrent requests. Consider consuming the code inside a transaction with a re-read (e.g., `prisma.$transaction` with serializable isolation) or verifying after update that the slot was still present.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup code plus any dummy TOTP code bypasses password verification at login

In the credentials authorize callback, the password check is gated on `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` (line 121): whenever a totpCode value is present, the password is never verified. The new backup-code branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` is evaluated before the TOTP branch, so an attacker can POST to the credentials callback with `email`, `backupCode=<valid code>`, and `totpCode=000000` (any non-empty value) and log in without knowing the account password. The web UI never sends both fields, but nothing server-side prevents it, so a backup code — intended as a second factor after the password — becomes a single-factor credential that fully bypasses the password. The fix should verify the password (when the user has one) regardless of whether totpCode or backupCode is supplied, or reject requests that contain both a backupCode and a totpCode.

Backup codes unusable for GOOGLE/SAML users who have 2FA enabled

The guard `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode) throw new Error(ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled)` runs before the backup-code branch. Users whose identity provider is GOOGLE or SAML but who have twoFactorEnabled — which the signIn callback itself can create by converting a CAL account with 2FA to Google/SAML (lines 693–706) — log in via the loginWithTotp flow, where the password field is empty. If such a user clicks 'Lost access' and submits a backup code, totpCode is empty, so they get ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled ('account_created_with_identity_provider') instead of the backup code being checked. These users can never use their backup codes and are locked out if they lose their authenticator. The identity-provider guards need to treat a supplied backupCode the same way as a totpCode.

Consumed backup codes are nulled in place instead of removed

After a successful backup-code login the code does `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypts the array, leaving permanent `null` holes in the stored list. As a result the array never shrinks: once all ten codes are used the stored value is still truthy, so the user gets IncorrectBackupCode forever instead of MissingBackupCodes, and the stored blob accumulates dead entries. Splicing the entry out (`backupCodes.splice(index, 1)`) would keep the data clean and let the existing MissingBackupCodes error fire correctly when the list is empty.

No test actually exercises logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code

The new e2e coverage only asserts that the backup-code screen appears after enabling 2FA and that the download/copy buttons work (with TODOs for the file and clipboard contents). The core security behavior added by this PR — that a backup code logs a user in, that it works only once, that the password is still required, and that disabling 2FA with a backup code works — is entirely untested (the author also checked 'I haven't added tests that prove my feature works', and the file itself carries a TODO for it). The password-bypass and non-CAL-provider issues above would have been caught by such tests; at minimum a login-with-backup-code test and a single-use (second attempt fails) test should be added before merging.

Parent 2FA switch state stays stale if the backup-codes dialog is dismissed without clicking Close

Previously `onEnable()` was called immediately when the enable request succeeded; this PR replaces that with `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` and only calls `onEnable()` from the 'Close' button on the backup-codes screen. If the user dismisses the dialog any other way after enabling (the dialog's X, clicking the overlay, or pressing Escape — all of which trigger onOpenChange), onEnable is never invoked, so the two-factor switch in settings remains visually unchecked even though 2FA is now enabled server-side, until a page reload. The dialog-close path should also fire onEnable (or the parent should refresh state on open change once enablement succeeded).

missing_backup_codes message tells users to 'generate them in your settings' but no such regeneration UI exists

The added copy for `missing_backup_codes` reads 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' This PR adds no way to regenerate backup codes from settings — codes are only created during the 2FA setup flow, so the only way to get new ones is to disable and re-enable 2FA (which itself may require a backup code in the lost-access flow). The message directs users to an action that doesn't exist; it should be reworded (e.g., instruct them to contact support or reconfigure two-factor authentication).

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback can never match, leaving calendarId undefined

In `updateEvent` the fallback was changed from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. This branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the find predicate compares each calendar's externalId against a falsy value and can never match — `selectedCalendar` is always `undefined`, and `calendarId: selectedCalendar` is passed to `calendar.events.update`, producing an API error and failing the update for any booking reference lacking `externalCalendarId`. The same dead fallback exists in `deleteEvent` (line ~317), where it now falls through to "primary" instead of the event's actual destination calendar, so deletes can target the wrong calendar.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unrelated change inverts IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition for org slug

This PR flips `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` (and similarly for `requestedSlug`) in the organization create handler — a semantic inversion unrelated to the destinationCalendar change. With the new condition, the org's `slug` is only written when team billing is enabled and is omitted when it is disabled (previously the opposite), so organizations created on instances without team billing will be missing their slug.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
CalDAV createEvent silently creates nothing for non-main hosts

In `BaseCalendarService.createEvent`, the calendar list is filtered by `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` where `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar`. When this service runs with a team member's CalDAV credential (per the new per-host creation loop in EventManager), the main host's calendar URL will not match any of the member's calendars, so the filtered array is empty, `Promise.all([])` succeeds, and the method returns a success result with a uid even though no event was written anywhere. This silently reports success while creating no calendar event for that host.

Crash when destinationCalendar is null/empty and location is Google Meet

In `EventManager.create`, the Google Meet fallback check was changed from `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` (null-safe) to `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. When the event has no destination calendar (which is common — `handleNewBooking` now sets `destinationCalendar: null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one) and the location is Meet, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and reading `.integration` throws a TypeError, crashing booking creation. The optional chaining on the destructured value was lost.

Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar regardless of credential

Same class of bug as Office365: `createEvent` (and `createAttendees`, `updateEvent`, `deleteEvent`) destructures only the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar`. Since `EventManager` now invokes `createEvent` once per host destination calendar with that host's credential, a Lark credential belonging to a non-main host will attempt to create the event in the main host's Lark calendar ID, which is not accessible/existent for that host's account, so the event creation fails for every non-primary host.

Office365 createEvent always uses the main host's calendar ID, breaking other hosts

With `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now creating one event per destination calendar using each host's own credential, `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` still takes only the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) and posts to `/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId}/events`. When this service instance belongs to a non-main host, that externalId is the main host's calendar ID, which does not exist in the team member's Office365 account, so creation fails (404) and that host never gets the event. Unlike the Google service, no matching by `credentialId` was added here.

Recurring-cancel deletion now runs once per calendar reference and only cleans the first reference of other bookings

The recurring-event deletion block (`if (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && ... allRemainingBookings)`) was moved inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop, so for a booking with N calendar references (now normal with multiple hosts) the entire recurring-deletion routine executes N times, issuing duplicate deletes of the same events. Additionally, within that block each updated recurring booking is processed via `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`, which only returns the first calendar reference — the other hosts' calendar events on those recurring instances are never deleted, leaving orphaned events in their calendars after a full-series cancellation.

Team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has no destination calendar

`evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. A few lines later, collective team members' calendars are added via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` — the optional chaining means the push is a no-op when the value is `null`, so all collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded. For a collective event whose organizer has no destination calendar but whose hosts do, no host receives a calendar event, which is exactly the bug this PR is meant to fix. The array should be initialized (e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`).

createEvent patch uses possibly-undefined calendarId after inserting into primary

In `createEvent`, the insert falls back to `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (used to add the hangout link to the description) still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` unmodified. When no destination calendar matches the credential (selectedCalendar is undefined), the event is created in the primary calendar but the patch request is issued with an undefined calendarId, so the hangout-link patch fails — and since the promise is not awaited or caught, it can also surface as an unhandled rejection.

loadUsers no longer selects organization.slug for dynamic user list

The rewritten `loadUsers` for dynamic group bookings drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the prisma select. Any downstream code that reads `user.organization.slug` for these users (e.g. booker URL / organization subdomain handling) will now receive `undefined`, silently changing behavior for dynamic bookings belonging to organization users. If the removal was intentional it should be verified against all consumers of the loaded users.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Literal "refresh_token" placeholder overwrites real refresh tokens in the DB

When the parsed token response has no `refresh_token`, the code invents one: `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. This runs in both modes, not just sync mode. In `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264` the parsed data is merged over the stored credentials (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`) and persisted, so if Microsoft's token endpoint omits `refresh_token` in a refresh response (which the schema explicitly allows via `.optional()`), the user's real refresh token in the database is replaced by the string "refresh_token". The next refresh then fails with invalid_grant and the user's calendar disconnects — a regression for existing Office 365 users even with credential syncing disabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys don't work — expiry fields are silently stripped

`[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` do not create zod catchalls: `z.string().toString()` evaluates to a constant string ("[object Object]"), so the schema is effectively just `{ access_token: z.string() }` plus a meaningless literal key. Because zod object schemas strip unknown keys by default, parsing a sync-endpoint response like `{ access_token, expires_in }` or the mutated Google credentials object drops every property except `access_token` — including the expiry. Consequence: in sync mode the credentials written to the DB (e.g. Google at `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97`) lose `expiry_date`, so the token is considered expired on every subsequent call and the expiry returned by the sync endpoint is never persisted. Zod's `.catchall()`/`.passthrough()` was presumably intended.

When credential sync is enabled this helper returns the unparsed `fetch` `Response` from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, but the fallback branch returns whatever each provider's refresh function returns (googleapis `res` with `.data`, an axios response with `.data`, a Hubspot token object). `refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)` expects the Cal.com user id as its third argument, which it sends to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. true_positives.matched_candidate:
Refreshed Salesforce tokens are saved but the stale access token is used

In `getClient`, the code fetches a fresh token set from Salesforce, validates it, and writes it to the DB (lines 75–99), but then constructs the `jsforce.Connection` with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token` and `instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url` — the old, possibly-expired credential values — instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.
